Maria R.: quick heads-up, onboarded magnet-16b-int4-hybrid to the staging runtime and ran the long-priming KV smoke suite :eyeglasses:
Aj S.: nice — any red flags?
Maria R.: one weirdness: when we hit ~64k tokens of prefix (dynamic workload), the KV swap path triggers and we see token-level drift vs fp16 baseline. small but consistent -- prob RoPE scaling mismatch after the swap.
Cheng L.: can you paste the failing prompt / short repro?
Maria R.: repro is noisy but consistent. command I used:
```bash
onboard-smoke --model magnet-16b-int4-hybrid --bench long-kv-suite --seed 42 --prefill 65536 --enable-kv-swap
```
Maria R.: observed diffs in final few tokens; deterministic run shows divergence at token index ~65540 (i.e. right after swap).
Oliver P.: reaction: :thinking_face: are you hitting an off-by-one in the rope index offset on the swap boundary?
Maria R.: that was my first guess. difflog excerpt (short):
```
[2026-03-21T10:02:12Z] PREFILL 65536 tokens -> warmhead complete
[2026-03-21T10:02:12Z] KV-SWAP start shard=1->2
[2026-03-21T10:02:12Z] KV-SWAP complete in 3ms
[2026-03-21T10:02:12Z] GENERATE token=65537 expected="ing" got="an"
```
Cheng L.: is this only with int4-hybrid quant? any repro with int8 or fp16?
Maria R.: int8 baseline = clean. fp16 = clean. int4-hybrid = reproducible. I tested both our local quant kernels and the fallback reference kernel; same behavior only when using the compact int4 cache packing + swap codepath.
Aj S.: could be packing/unpacking alignment when we stitch KV chunks during swap. maybe padding bytes lost?
Oliver P.: also check rotary scaling factors — int4 packer uses a different scale table, we were lazy and reused the shard-global rot_scale instead of recomputing per-chunk.
Maria R.: good call. I added a debug assert to compare rot_scale before/after swap and it fails on ~1/10000 swaps in the fuzz harness.
Maria R.: quick patch to recompute rot_scale on unpack pushed to my branch: "maria/kv-rescale-unpack". running overnight fuzz now.
qa-bot: scheduled long-kv-fuzz on branch maria/kv-rescale-unpack (job id: 2026-03-21-0892), ETA 6h.
Cheng L.: if that fixes it we should add a unit test that simulates a swap boundary with deterministic random padding patterns.
Maria R.: adding test now — low-effort harness: produce two chunks with different token counts, pack into int4 buffer, unpack and compare to fp32 reference.
Aj S.: unrelated note: we saw a perf regression on throughput when enabling dynamic KV-swap thresholds on Dedicated — 4% loss. file a perf ticket?
Oliver P.: yes please. but prioritize correctness first. after rescale fix, we can profile the swap hot path.
Maria R.: update: after recomputing rot_scale on unpack, the smoke run produced identical tokens up to 128k prefill (ran to 131072). no divergence so far. pushing PR for review.
ci-bot: PR maria/kv-rescale-unpack -> staging: run tests (smoke,long-kv-suite,unit-kv) queued.
Aj S.: awesome. when PR lands, let's run the quant benchmark matrix (int4-hybrid vs int8 vs fp16) across 16k/64k/131k prefill. capture token-diff and latency percentiles.
Maria R.: agreed. I'll add a small CSV writer to the harness to record token-diff counts + p50/p95/p99 latency.
Cheng L.: also add a quick check for "kv-swapped=true" in logs to correlate with diffs.
Maria R.: done. test plan linked in PR description. thanks all :thumbsup:
Oliver P.: once green, schedule a canary on a tiny subset of dedicated nodes, but with aggressive logging disabled (only diffs).
Maria R.: will do. closing the loop on this thread when canary finishes.
ci-bot: job maria/kv-rescale-unpack long-kv-suite passed (job id: 2026-03-22-1123)
Maria R.: CI passed. moving to canary tomorrow.
Oliver P.: great work, saved us from a subtle regression. :party_popper:
